titleEn: Book of the Dead of Ani — Spell 18, the tribunals, sections F–J
part: Spell 18 — the tribunals, sections F–J and the rubric (Plate 14)
about: Plate 14 of Ani's papyrus carries the second half of Spell 18, after sections A–E on Plate 13. In five more sections, each opened in red, the spell names the tribunal at Abydos, at the judging of the dead, at the hacking up of the earth in Busiris, in En-iarered-ef and in Rosetau, and explains a night of the story of Osiris: the inspecting of the condemned, the slaughter of Seth's band, the burial of the god's limbs. Between them the refrain asks Thoth to make Ani true of voice, at the end before all ten tribunals together, and a closing rubric in red promises that the one over whom the spell is recited comes forth by day and escapes every fire. Several rare words in this part are doubtful, and the notes say where.

sentences.l: as-for · the-tribunal · great · which-is-in · Abydos · Osiris · it-is · Isis · it-is · Wepwawet · it-is
sentences.i: As for the great tribunal which is in Abydos: it is Osiris, Isis and Wepwawet.
sentences.n: Plate 14 begins here, and with it Budge's section F; as in sections A–E, his line numerals start again at 1 in each of the sections F–J. The papyrus writes ir ḏꜣḏꜣt ꜥꜣt imyt ꜣbḏw in red; the gods are black. The opening is the one of every section on Plate 13: ir 'as for', ḏꜣḏꜣt 'tribunal' (the fire-drill ḏꜣ twice, coded U28, with a small ring, t and a barred sign, coded W24 and N1, approximate, and the god and a stroke), ꜥꜣt 'great' with the roll after it, and imyt 'which is in' (the reed, im and t). ꜣbḏw 'Abydos' is spelled as in the last refrain of Plate 13: the ankh-like sign (coded S34, approximate) for ꜣb, the foot b, the low sign ḏw (coded N26) and the town sign, with the chick w written after the town sign. ꜣst 'Isis' is the seat, t, the egg and the cobra (coded I12, approximate). wp-wꜣwt is the horns wp (F13), a sign of a road on a stand (coded N31, approximate) for wꜣt 'way', with t, two strokes and the seated god: 'Opener of the Ways' (Budge: Àp-uat), the jackal god who goes before Osiris. Abydos is the holy city of Osiris, where his tomb was shown; its tribunal is the one the last refrain of Plate 13 named.

sentences.l: O · Thoth · who-makes-true-of-voice · Osiris · against · enemies-his
sentences.i: O Thoth, who makes Osiris true of voice against his enemies,
sentences.n: The papyrus writes i in red. The refrain of the spell, written as on Plate 13: i 'O' with the man with hand to mouth, ḏḥwty 'Thoth', the participle smꜣꜥ-ḫrw 'who makes true of voice' in full, wsir, r 'against' and ḫftyw·f 'his enemies', its vulture not read. Budge's numeral 2 is printed inside smꜣꜥ-ḫrw, after the plinth, and the line is kept at 1.

sentences.l: make-true-of-voice · the-Osiris · the-scribe · accounting · of-the-god's-offerings · of · gods · all · Ani · against · enemies-his · before · the-tribunal · of-the-judging · of-the-dead
sentences.i: make the Osiris, the accounting scribe of the god's offerings of all the gods, Ani, true of voice against his enemies before the tribunal of the judging of the dead
sentences.n: smꜣꜥ-ḫrw is here the imperative, written in full with the classifier. Ani's titles stand between wsir and his name: sš 'scribe' (the palette, Y3) and ḥsb 'accounting' (a tilted oval with two small arcs, coded Aa2, approximate, with the roll), together sš ḥsb 'accounting scribe'. ḥtp-nṯr 'the god's offerings' is the loaf on a mat ḥtp (R4) with t and p as complements, then the flag nṯr with the seated god; Budge prints ḥtp and nṯr as two groups, and they are joined here as the one word they make. n nṯrw nbw 'of all the gods' is water n, the flag three times for the plural, and the basket nb with plural strokes. ꜣny has the squatting man with a flail (A52) as classifier. On Plate 13 the refrain names the next tribunal as 'the great tribunal which is in' a place; here it names it by an event, ḏꜣḏꜣt wpwt mtw, with neither ꜥꜣt nor imyt. wpwt is the horns wp (F13) with p as complement, w and t, with crossed sticks (Z9) and the man with hand to mouth as classifiers: taken as the infinitive of wpi 'part, separate, judge between', 'the judging', its w written (Budge: àput, 'judge'). mtw 'the dead' is m, t and w with the kneeling captive (coded A13, approximate) and a stroke, as on Plate 13: the dead who are condemned. Section G opens with the same tribunal, 'which is at the judging of the dead'.

sentences.l: night · that · of · making · the-inspecting · of-the-condemned(?)-their
sentences.i: on that night of carrying out the inspecting of their condemned(?).
sentences.n: grḥ pwy n 'that night of', as on Plate 13; Budge's numeral 4 falls inside pwy, after p, and the line is kept at 3. irt 'making' is the eye ir with t, the infinitive of iri. sipt 'the inspecting' is the folded cloth s, the reed, p and t with the roll, as at the end of Plate 13. mnty·sn is the owl m, water n, t and the vulture ꜣ, with the kneeling captive (coded A13, approximate) and a stroke, then ·sn 'their', here the folded cloth s, water n and plural strokes; Budge prints ·sn as a group of its own, and it is joined to its noun here. The vulture after t is taken as in ḫftyw 'enemies', which this papyrus spells ḫ f t ꜣ with the same captive, an old spelling in which ꜣ is not read; in section G the word has two strokes y as well, mnty. The word is not known in these parts. The captive classes the people it names with enemies, and Budge renders 'those who are annihilated'; it is rendered 'condemned' with a query. ·sn 'their' perhaps refers to the dead just named. The inspecting of the dead sorts out those who are to be destroyed.

sentences.l: as-for · the-tribunal · great · which-is-in · the-judging · of-the-dead · Thoth · it-is · Osiris · it-is · Anubis · it-is · Isdenu · it-is
sentences.i: As for the great tribunal which is at the judging of the dead: it is Thoth, Osiris, Anubis and Isdenu.
sentences.n: Section G begins, and Budge's line numerals start again at 1. The papyrus writes ir ḏꜣḏꜣt ꜥꜣt imyt wpt mtw in red; the gods are black. ꜥꜣt has the roll after it. wpt 'the judging' is the horns wp with p, the crossed sticks and the man with hand to mouth, its t not written; mtw as in the refrain. inpw 'Anubis' is the reed, n, p and w with a jackal lying on a shrine (E16) as classifier. isdnw is the reed, the folded cloth s, the hand d, water n and the pot nw (coded W24) with the seated god (Budge: Àsṭennu); Budge's numeral 2 is printed before the pot, and the line is kept at 1. The name is close to that of Isdes (isds), a god of the judgement whom Spell 17 names beside Thoth, and it may be the same god, but the spelling differs. With Thoth, Osiris and Anubis he makes up the court that judges the dead.

sentences.l: as-for · the-inspecting · of-the-condemned(?)-their · are-shut-away(?) · things · it-is · on-account-of · the-bas · of · the-children · of-weakness
sentences.i: As for the inspecting of their condemned(?): it is that things are shut away(?) on account of the bas of the children of weakness.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ir sipt mnty·sn in red. Each 'ir …' unit in this spell takes up the night named at the end of the section before, and this one explains the inspecting named at the end of section F. mnty·sn is the same word as there, written here with two strokes y after t, and with ·sn (the bolt s, water n and strokes) in the same group. ḫnr·tw is the placenta ḫ, water n and the reed, then a low sign with a fringed end and a long line (coded U15, approximate) as classifier, t and the chick w. No r is written: the reed stands where r is expected, and Budge too reads no r (χenà-tu, 'the imprisonment'). Spell 1 writes ḫnr 'restrain, shut in' ḫ n r, with the reed and the low hooked sign among its classifiers, and the word is read as ḫnr; the low sign, which here looks like an enclosure, suits that sense as a classifier, but nothing shows that it writes ḫnr by itself. The tw after it is the passive sḏm·tw·f: '(things) are shut away'. The reading is doubtful. ḫt 'things' is ḫ and t with the roll and a stroke. pw after the clause makes it the explanation: 'it is (that) …'. ḥr is taken as 'on account of'. bꜣw 'the bas' is the jabiru bꜣ (G29) with a small pot (coded R7) at its foot and two strokes; nw 'of' is the pot nw, the genitive n in its plural form. msw 'the children' is the three skins ms (F31) with s, w and a stroke. bdšt is the foot b, the hand d, a rectangle with a slanting double line (coded N37, approximate) for š, t, a small looped cord (coded V1, approximate) and a stroke: bdšt 'weakness', from bdš 'be weak, faint' (Budge: beṭeśet, 'impotent rebellion'). 'The children of weakness' are the enemies of Osiris; what the shutting away of things does to them is not said.

sentences.l: O · Thoth · who-makes-true-of-voice · Osiris · against · enemies-his
sentences.i: O Thoth, who makes Osiris true of voice against his enemies,
sentences.n: The papyrus writes i in red, at the end of line 2. The refrain again; ḏḥwty is printed small after Budge's numeral 3, and smꜣꜥ-ḫrw has no chick w.

sentences.l: make-true-of-voice · the-Osiris · the-scribe · Ani · true-of-voice · against · enemies-his · before · the-tribunal · great · which-is-in · the-hacking-up-of-the-earth · in · Busiris
sentences.i: make true of voice the Osiris, the scribe Ani, true of voice, against his enemies before the great tribunal which is at the hacking up of the earth in Busiris
sentences.n: smꜣꜥ-ḫrw is the imperative, again without w. mꜣꜥ-ḫrw after the name is the plinth over the oar, without the sickle, as on Plate 13. ꜥꜣt has no roll here. ḫbs-tꜣ is the placenta ḫ and the foot b, a plough-like sign (coded U13, approximate) beside the low hooked sign (U15) as classifiers, the bolt s, and the flat land sign tꜣ (coded N16, approximate): ḫbs 'hack up, break up (the ground)' with tꜣ 'the earth' as its object, one group in Budge, kept here as one word of two parts (Budge: χebs-ta, '[the festival of] breaking and turning up the earth'). m ḏdw 'in Busiris': the owl and the djed pillar twice with w and the town sign. The hacking up of the earth, the hoeing of the ground, was a rite of Osiris at Busiris, and its tribunal is the one section H explains.

sentences.l: night · that · of · hacking-up-the-earth · in · blood-their · making-true-of-voice · Osiris · against · enemies-his
sentences.i: on that night of hacking up the earth in their blood, and of making Osiris true of voice against his enemies.
sentences.n: ḫbs-tꜣ is written as in the refrain, here with the plough set above the low sign. m 'in' is the owl. snf·sn is the bolt s, water n and the viper f with two strokes and a stem with a zigzag rising from it (coded D26, approximate), the classifier of blood, and a stroke, then ·sn: snf 'blood', 'their blood'. Whose blood it is is not said; 'their' perhaps points back to the children of weakness of section G. smꜣꜥ-ḫrw, without w, is here the infinitive, a second noun after the same n 'of', 'making true of voice', a second event of the same night. The night joins the hoeing of the earth to the defeat of the enemies of Osiris.

sentences.l: as-for · the-tribunal · great · which-is-in · the-hacking-up-of-the-earth · in · Busiris · the-coming · of-the-confederates · of-Seth · it-is · had-made-they · forms-their · as · small-cattle
sentences.i: As for the great tribunal which is at the hacking up of the earth in Busiris: it is the coming of the confederates of Seth, when they had taken on the form of small cattle.
sentences.n: Section H begins, and Budge's line numerals start again at 1. The papyrus writes ir ḏꜣḏꜣt ꜥꜣt imyt ḫbs-tꜣ m ḏdw in red. Where the other sections name the gods of the tribunal, this one goes straight to what happened there. iwt 'the coming' is the chick w and t between two small carets, both coded D54, the walking legs (the first approximate): the infinitive of iwi 'come'. The first sign stands where the legs with a reed, ii, would be expected; as printed, the i is not written. smꜣyw 'the confederates' is the lungs and windpipe smꜣ (coded F36, approximate) with ꜣ, two reeds, the coil w (Z7), and the low hooked sign (U15) with a stroke as classifiers (Budge: samiu, 'fiends'); stẖ 'Seth' is s, t, the rectangle (coded N37, approximate) and the god, as on Plate 13. ir·n·sn is the eye ir, water n and ·sn: the sḏm·n·f, 'they had made'; Budge prints three groups, joined here as one verb form. ḫprw·sn 'their forms' is the scarab ḫpr with r and w, the roll and a stroke, then ·sn; Budge's numeral 2 is printed before ·sn, and the line is kept at 1. iri ḫprw m 'make one's forms as' is to take on a shape. ꜥwt is the shepherd's crook (coded S39, approximate), which writes ꜥwt, with w and t, and a hide over plural strokes as classifier: 'small cattle, flocks', the goats and sheep (Budge: āut, 'animals'). Seth's band came to the rite disguised as beasts of the flock, and the next sentence tells how they ended.

sentences.l: then-they · slaughtered · in-the-presence-of · (ꜥ) · gods · these
sentences.i: Then they were slaughtered in the presence of these gods.
sentences.n: ꜥḥꜥ·n·sn is the mast ꜥḥꜥ (P6) with the arm ꜥ as complement (printed as a low bar with a tab and no roll, coded D36), water n and ·sn: ꜥḥꜥ·n 'then', the auxiliary that opens a narrative sentence, with 'they' as its subject. Budge prints three groups and gives ꜥḥꜥ·n no English; they are joined here. sft is the folded cloth s, f and t with a knife (coded T30, approximate) and the low hooked sign as classifiers: sft 'slaughter, butcher', after ꜥḥꜥ·n·sn the stative, '(were) slaughtered'. m-bꜣḥ 'in the presence of' is the owl m and the phallus sign bꜣḥ (D53) with a stroke and the roll. After it stands the arm ꜥ with a stroke, here and again in section J, with no English in Budge. It is not explained (perhaps a fuller writing of the preposition), and it is left untranslated. nṯrw ipw 'these gods' is the flag three times and ipw, the reed, p and w with the roll and a stroke. 'These gods' are the gods of the tribunal.

sentences.l: not · could-be-stopped(?) · the-blood · going-down · among-them
sentences.i: The blood could not be stopped(?), running down among them.
sentences.n: n is water n, taken as the negative before the passive sḏm·n·tw·f: 'it could not be …' (Budge takes it as 'and'). ḏri·n·tw is a tied bundle (coded M36, approximate), ḏr, with r as complement and the reed, then an arm (coded D41, approximate) and the low hooked sign as classifiers, water n, t and w: the passive of the past of a verb from ḏr 'end, limit', taken as 'put an end to, stop', which the arm, the classifier of holding back, suits (Budge: t'erà-entu, 'being smitten down'). The reading is doubtful. snf 'blood' is written as in section G, here with plural strokes and no suffix (Budge: senf-u, 'their blood'). hꜣy is the reed-shelter h, ꜣ, two reeds, two strokes and the walking legs: hꜣi 'go down', spelled as in Spell 17, here 'going down, running'. im·sn 'among them' is the reed and the owl m, the form im that the preposition m takes before a suffix, with ·sn. The slaughter of Seth's band at the hoeing explains the blood of the night in section G.

sentences.l: was-granted(?) · by · the-inspecting · of · those-who-are-in · Busiris
sentences.i: It was granted(?) by the inspecting of those who are in Busiris.
sentences.n: rdi·n·tw is the mouth r and the arm (D36), which this papyrus writes for the hand that gives, as in Spell 1, then the chick w, water n, t, w and a stroke: rdi 'give, grant' in the passive of the past, 'it was given, granted'. The w after the arm is not read. Budge's numeral 3 is printed after the first w, and the line is kept at 2. What was granted is not said, and m 'by' is taken as naming the authority that granted it. sipt 'the inspecting' has a stroke after the roll here. imyw 'those who are in' is the reed, im with the owl m, w and a stroke; ḏdw 'Busiris' has the town sign before w. Perhaps the gods of Busiris, by their inspecting, allowed the slaughter; the text does not say so.

sentences.l: O · Thoth · who-makes-true-of-voice · Osiris · against · enemies-his
sentences.i: O Thoth, who makes Osiris true of voice against his enemies,
sentences.n: The papyrus writes i in red. The refrain again; ḏḥwty is here the ibis on its standard alone, without t and the strokes, and smꜣꜥ-ḫrw is written in full.

sentences.l: make-true-of-voice · the-Osiris · Ani · against · enemies-his · before · the-tribunal · great · which-is-in · En-iarered-ef
sentences.i: make the Osiris Ani true of voice against his enemies before the great tribunal which is in En-iarered-ef
sentences.n: smꜣꜥ-ḫrw is the imperative, in full. ꜣny follows Budge's numeral 4 and has as classifier a kneeling man with one arm raised (A1), not the squatting man with the flail. ꜥꜣt has no roll. n-iꜣrrd-f is spelled as in section C on Plate 13: water n, the vulture and the reed, r twice, a cord with tails (coded T12, approximate) for rd, an open box (coded O1) as classifier and the viper f (Budge: Naàrereṭef). The refrain names the tribunal of section I, in the holy place of Osiris named in Spell 17.

sentences.l: night · that · of · hiding · the-forms
sentences.i: on that night of hiding the forms.
sentences.n: sštꜣ is the bolt s, the rectangle with a slanting double line (coded N37, approximate) for š, t, a cup-shaped sign with a rim (coded W10, approximate), the vulture ꜣ, and crossed sticks and the roll as classifiers: sštꜣ 'hide, make secret', the infinitive (Budge: seśeta, 'making secret'). The cup-shaped sign is not identified and is not read. irw 'the forms' is the reed, the eye ir with r and w, the standing mummy (A53), the roll and a stroke, the classifiers of irw 'form, shape' in Spell 17. Section I says what forms were hidden.

sentences.l: as-for · the-tribunal · great · which-is-in · En-iarered-ef · Ra · it-is · Osiris · it-is · Shu · it-is · Babi · it-is
sentences.i: As for the great tribunal which is in En-iarered-ef: it is Ra, Osiris, Shu and Babi.
sentences.n: Section I begins, and Budge's line numerals start again at 1. The papyrus writes ir ḏꜣḏꜣt ꜥꜣt imyt n-iꜣrrd-f in red. ꜥꜣt has t printed before the arm here. n-iꜣrrd-f is written as in the refrain. rꜥ 'Ra' is the sun with a stroke and the seated god. šw 'Shu' is the feather šw with w, without the god. bby is the foot b twice and two reeds with the god (Budge: Bebi): the baboon god Babi, written here without the vulture; the published parts say his name Babi. Ra the sun and Shu the air sit here with Osiris and the savage Babi.

sentences.l: as-for · night · that · of · hiding · the-forms · is-one · at · burying · the-foreleg · the-side(?) · the-thigh(?) · of · Osiris · Wennefer
sentences.i: As for that night of hiding the forms: one is burying the foreleg, the side(?) and the thigh(?) of Osiris Wennefer.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes ir grḥ pwy n sštꜣ irw in red. sštꜣ has plural strokes after the roll; Budge's numeral 2 is printed inside it, and the line is kept at 1. wnn·tw is the hare wn (E34) with water n twice, t and w: wnn 'be' with ·tw 'one', 'one is'; with ḥr and an infinitive it says what one is busy doing. qrs is the hill-slope q (N29, approximate), r and the bolt s, with a coffin (coded Q6, approximate) and the low hooked sign as classifiers: qrs 'bury', the infinitive (Budge: qeres, 'the sarcophagus'). On Plate 13 the same signs are the noun qrsw 'coffin'; after ḥr the verb is the better reading. ḫpš 'the foreleg' is ḫ, p and the rectangle (coded N37, approximate) for š, a wavy band (coded F23, approximate), a stroke, a curled sign of flesh (coded F51, approximate) and the seated god, here the god's own limb. ḏrww is the tied bundle ḏr (coded M36, approximate), w twice and the seated god, perhaps a plural or dual. The word is not known in these parts; from ḏr 'limit, end' it is taken as 'side' with a query (Budge: t'eruu, 'heel'). mnt is the gaming board mn (Y5), n and t, with a lower leg (coded D56, approximate) and the god: by its classifier a word for the thigh or the leg (Budge: ment, 'leg'), not the adverb mnt 'daily'. n 'of' is the genitive. wnn-nfr 'Wennefer' is the hare wn, n twice, the heart and windpipe nfr and the god (Budge: Un-nefer). The body of Osiris was torn apart by Seth, and the forms hidden on this night are the parts of it laid in the ground.

sentences.l: O · Thoth · who-makes-true-of-voice · Osiris · against · enemies-his
sentences.i: O Thoth, who makes Osiris true of voice against his enemies,
sentences.n: The papyrus writes i in red. The refrain again; smꜣꜥ-ḫrw has no chick w.

sentences.l: make-true-of-voice · the-Osiris · Ani · true-of-voice · before · Osiris · against · enemies-his · before · the-tribunal · great · which-is-in · Rosetau
sentences.i: make true of voice the Osiris Ani, true of voice before Osiris, against his enemies before the great tribunal which is in Rosetau
sentences.n: mꜣꜥ-ḫrw ḫr wsir 'true of voice before Osiris': mꜣꜥ-ḫrw is again without the sickle, and ḫr is the placenta ḫ and r, the preposition 'with, before' used of persons. ḫftyw·f is written here without the vulture. ꜥꜣt has the roll; two faint ticks after its t are taken as broken type. rꜣ-sṯꜣw 'Rosetau', after Budge's numeral 4, is the mouth rꜣ with a stroke, a rope sign (coded V2, approximate) for sṯꜣ, t and plural strokes, and a crenellated sign (coded N25, approximate) as classifier, as in the introduction: the necropolis of Sokar near Giza, here a realm of the dead. The refrain names the tribunal of section J.

sentences.l: night · that · of · lying-down · of-Anubis · arms-his-two · upon · the-things · behind · Osiris · making-true-of-voice · Horus · against · enemies-his
sentences.i: on that night of Anubis's lying down with his arms upon the things behind Osiris, and of making Horus true of voice against his enemies.
sentences.n: A small speck after grḥ is not read. sḏr 'lying down' is s, the tied bundle ḏr (coded M36, approximate) with r, and a bed with a lion's head and tail, here empty (coded A55, approximate): the infinitive, with inpw after it as its subject, as with Isis on Plate 13. inpw is written as in section G. ꜥwy·fy 'his two arms' is the arm (D36) twice with a stroke, two strokes y and w, the dual ꜥwy, then the viper with two strokes, ·fy, the suffix made dual to agree with the arms. ḥr 'upon' is the face with its stroke. ḫt 'the things' is ḫ, t, the roll and a stroke; what things are meant is not said. ḥꜣ 'behind' is the papyrus clump ḥꜣ with a small head (D1), as on Plate 13. smꜣꜥ-ḫrw, without w, is again the infinitive, a second noun after the same n 'of', with ḥr 'Horus', the falcon and the god, as its object. Anubis, the embalmer, keeps watch over the body of Osiris, and Horus, his son, wins his case.

sentences.l: as-for · the-tribunal · great · which-is-in · Rosetau · Horus · it-is · Osiris · it-is · Isis · it-is
sentences.i: As for the great tribunal which is in Rosetau: it is Horus, Osiris and Isis.
sentences.n: Section J, the last, begins, and Budge's line numerals start again at 1. The papyrus writes ir ḏꜣḏꜣt ꜥꜣt imyt rꜣ-sṯꜣw in red. ꜥꜣt has the roll, and rꜣ-sṯꜣw is written as in the refrain. ḥr 'Horus' is the falcon alone; ꜣst 'Isis' has the egg and the cobra.

sentences.l: (iw) · Osiris · heart-his · is-sweet · (iw) · Horus · heart-his · is-long · (iw) · the-Two-Shrines · are-content · with-it
sentences.i: The heart of Osiris is glad, the heart of Horus is joyful, and the Two Shrines are content with it.
sentences.n: Three short clauses, each opened by iw, the reed and the chick w, which is not translated. Each puts its subject first and then says how its heart is: 'Osiris, his heart is sweet'. ib·f 'his heart' is the heart (F34) with its stroke and the viper ·f. nḏm is a twisted pod (coded M29; in print close to the wick ḥ) with the owl m as complement and the roll: nḏm 'be sweet, pleasant', here the stative; a sweet heart is a glad one. ꜣw is a hatched sign with a loop at each end (coded F40, approximate), ꜣw, with w and the roll: ꜣw 'be long', the stative; to be 'long of heart' (ꜣw ib) is the Egyptian for joy. The second ib·f begins Budge's line 2. itrty is the reed, t, r, t and two strokes y, with two shrines (printed as open boxes, coded O1) as classifier: itrty 'the Two Shrines', the national shrines of Upper and Lower Egypt, standing for the gods of the whole land. ḥtp·ti is the loaf on a mat ḥtp with t and p, then t and w: ḥtp 'be content' in the stative, its ending written tw, as with Isis on Plate 13. ḥr·s 'with it' is the face ḥr with r and the bolt ·s; the 'it' is feminine and is not named, perhaps the outcome of the case. The joy is for the verdict won for Osiris and Horus.

sentences.l: O · Thoth · who-makes-true-of-voice · Osiris · against · enemies-his
sentences.i: O Thoth, who makes Osiris true of voice against his enemies,
sentences.n: The papyrus writes i in red. The refrain for the last time; ḏḥwty is printed small, and smꜣꜥ-ḫrw is in full.

sentences.l: make-true-of-voice · the-Osiris · the-scribe · accounting · of-the-god's-offerings · of · gods · all · Ani · true-of-voice · against · enemies-his
sentences.i: make true of voice the Osiris, the accounting scribe of the god's offerings of all the gods, Ani, true of voice, against his enemies
sentences.n: smꜣꜥ-ḫrw is the imperative, in full; Budge's numeral 3 is printed before its last sign, and the line is kept at 2. Ani's titles are as in section F, with ḥtp and nṯr again joined as one word; nṯrw 'the gods' is written here with the flag, the seated god and a stroke, not the flag three times. mꜣꜥ-ḫrw is without the sickle.

sentences.l: before · the-tribunal(s) · great · ten · which-are-with · Ra · which-are-with · Osiris · which-are-with · god · every · goddess · every · in-the-presence-of · (ꜥ) · the-Lord-to-the-Limit
sentences.i: before the ten great tribunals which are with Ra, with Osiris, and with every god and every goddess, in the presence of the Lord to the Limit.
sentences.n: The last refrain names not one tribunal but all of them. After ḏꜣḏꜣt ꜥꜣt (Budge's numeral 4 falls before ꜥꜣt) stands the sign for ten (V20), mḏ, the number after its noun, which is written without a plural ending. The tribunals of the spell are ten: Heliopolis, Busiris, Sekhem, Pe and Dep, the Banks of Rekhty, Abydos, the judging of the dead, the hacking up of the earth, En-iarered-ef and Rosetau. imyt 'which is in' is used three times before the names of gods: 'which are with, which belong to'. nṯr nb 'every god' is the flag and the seated god with the basket; nṯrt 'goddess' is the flag with t, r and t, the t that follows the flag standing for its ṯ, and nbt 'every' is feminine to agree. m-bꜣḥ is written as in section H, again with the arm ꜥ after it, left untranslated. nb-r-ḏr is the basket nb, r, the tied bundle ḏr (coded M36, approximate) with r and the god: 'the Lord to the Limit', the lord of all that is (Budge: Neb-er-tcher).

sentences.l: drives-off-he · enemies-his · drives-off-he · evil · all · which-belongs-to-him
sentences.i: He drives off his enemies, he drives off every evil that belongs to him.
sentences.n: dr·f is the hand d and r with the low hooked sign as classifier and the viper: dr 'drive off, repel' in the sḏm·f, 'he drives off'. The second dr·f begins Budge's line 5. Who 'he' is is not said: the Lord to the Limit, or Ani himself. ḏwt 'evil' is the mountain ḏw (N26) with t and w, the sparrow of bad things and plural strokes. nbt 'all' is feminine to agree. irt·f is the reed and r with t, a seated man wrapped in a cloak holding a stick (coded A47, approximate), the roll and a stroke, then ·f: the feminine of iry 'belonging to', 'which belongs to him'; the cloaked man is the sign of the keeper, iry. Here the text of the spell ends; the rest is its rubric.

sentences.l: is-said · spell · this · being-pure(?) · coming-forth · it-is · by · day · after · mooring · (in)-the-likeness · that-gives · heart-his
sentences.i: If this spell is said by one who is pure(?), it is a coming forth by day after mooring, in the likeness that his heart gives.
sentences.n: From ḏd·tw to the end, the papyrus writes the closing rubric of the spell in red. ḏd·tw is the cobra ḏ and the hand d (printed as one group), t and w: ḏd 'say' with ·tw 'one', 'one says, it is said'; at the head of a rubric this form states the condition, 'if this spell is said'. rꜣ pn 'this spell' is the mouth with its stroke and pn, p and n. wꜥb is the vase pouring water on a foot (D60) alone: 'pure', taken as said of the one who recites, 'being pure' (Budge reads it as the subject, 'the pure one'). pr pw m hrw 'it is a coming forth by day' is the house pr with r and the walking legs, pw, m, and hrw 'day', the reed-shelter h, r, w, the sun and a stroke: the phrase that names the whole book, here said of what the spell brings about. m-ḫt 'after' is the owl and the branch ḫt (coded M3, approximate) with ḫ and t and the walking legs. mni 'mooring' is the gaming board mn with n, the reed, a mooring post (coded P11, approximate) and a boat (coded P3, approximate): mni 'moor, come to land', said of the dead whose voyage of life is over. twt is t, the coil w, t, the seated god and the roll: twt 'image, likeness'. No verb or preposition is written before it (Budge supplies '[and he maketh]'), and it is taken as saying in what form he comes forth. dd, the first word of Budge's line 6, is the arm with a loaf (D37) twice, d d: the relative form of rdi 'give', 'which … gives', with ib·f 'his heart' as its subject. He comes forth in whatever shape his heart grants him.

sentences.l: if · (ḫr) · is-recited · spell · this · whole · over-him · prospering(?) · it-is · what-has-done-he · upon · earth
sentences.i: If this whole spell is recited over him, he prospers(?) upon earth.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes this in red. ir 'if' is the reed and the mouth. ḫr is the butcher's block (coded T28), which writes ẖr, with r and the roll; it is taken as the particle ḫr, which marks a further case or a consequence, and is left untranslated (Budge renders ir ḫr together, 'if'). The reading is doubtful. šdd·w is a looped cord with a trailing end (coded V6, approximate), the hand d twice, the coil w and the low hooked sign: taken as šd 'recite, read out', with its d doubled, in the passive with w, 'is recited' (Budge: seśeṭṭu, 'be recited'). Spell 1 writes šd with the water-skin šd, and the looped cord stands where that sign is expected; the reading rests on the sense. nb after pn is 'all, whole'. ḥr·f 'over him' is the face with its stroke and ·f. wḏꜣ is the chick w, the fire-drill ḏꜣ (U28) with ꜣ and the roll: wḏꜣ 'be sound, prosper', here the infinitive. ir·n·f is the eye, water n and ·f, one group: the relative form of the past, 'what he has done'. An infinitive with pw and ir·n·f is the set construction 'what he did was to …', which simply states the action, so wḏꜣ pw ir·n·f is 'he prospers', literally 'prospering is what he has done' (Budge takes it as 'it makes him strong'). wḏꜣ could also be the verb 'proceed, go on', 'he goes on upon earth', though it has the roll here and not the walking legs; the sense is doubtful. tp tꜣ 'upon earth' is the head tp with its stroke and the land sign twice (coded N16, approximate); tp tꜣ is the set phrase, but the doubled sign could also write tꜣwy 'the Two Lands'.

sentences.l: (iw)-he · comes-forth-he · from · fire · every · not · goes-round · him · thing · any · evil · any · which-belongs-to-him
sentences.i: He comes forth from every fire, and no thing, no evil that is his, goes round him.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes this in red. iw·f is the particle iw with ·f, and pr·f is pri in the sḏm·f with ·f again: 'he comes forth'. m 'from' is the sign m (Aa15). ḫt 'fire' is ḫ and t with a brazier with a flame (coded Q7, approximate) as classifier, and nbt 'every' is feminine to agree. n 'not' is the arms held out (coded D35, approximate) with water n: the negative before the sḏm·f. rr is a ring (coded V10, approximate) and r, with the walking legs as classifier: rr 'go round, encircle', as Budge reads it (rer), spelled as in Spells 17 and 147, where the ring writes the first r. sw 'him' is the sedge sw (M23) with the coil w: the dependent pronoun, the object. ḫt nb 'any thing' is ḫ and t with the basket; ḏwt nbt 'any evil' is ḏw (N26), t and the sparrow, without w or strokes here, then nb with t. iry·f is spelled as irt·f in the last section, but with two strokes y and no t: iry 'belonging to' with ·f. Fire is one of the dangers of the world below that the spells guard against.

sentences.l: truly(?) · right · a-million · times
sentences.i: Truly right, a million times.
sentences.n: The papyrus writes this in red. The rubric ends with a guarantee. šs is a tied bag (V33) with a stroke, taken as šs 'truly, properly' (the sense is not sure); mꜣꜥt 'right' is the plinth mꜣꜥ and t. ḥḥ 'a million' is the kneeling god with raised arms (C11), and sp 'times' is the bolt s, p and the threshing floor (O50): 'a million times', that is, it has never failed. Spell 18 ends here; Plate 15 goes on with Spells 23 and 24.
